newsitem.title: USA: Federated Dept Stores promotes president to top spot.
newsitem.headline: Federated Dept Stores promotes president to top spot.

text.p: Federated Department Stores Inc. Thursday said its president, James Zimmerman, 52, will take the helm from Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Allen Questrom who will leave office in May.

Questrom, 57, engineered Cincinnati-based Federated's transformation into the largest U.S. department store company. When he took over as chairman and CEO in 1990, Federated was in bankruptcy proceedings. It emerged from bankruptcy in 1992, acquired R.H. Macy & Co. in 1994, then California's Broadway Stores Inc. in 1995.
Federated's stores also include Bloomingdale's, The Bon Marche, Burdines, Goldsmith's, Lazarus, Rich's and Stern's.
In the year ended February 1996, net income was $332.8 million, or $1.82 a share, on $15 billion in sales.
Questrom has been with Federated 30 years. He joined another company in 1988 but returned as chairman in 1990.
The company's stock closed off 75 cents on the New York Stock Exchange at $30.875. Analysts said they did not foresee changes in corporate strategy since Zimmerman helped design it.
